players.product: Foundation models (MiniMax M3 language / agentic model, MiniMax H3 open-weight video generation) served through its Open Platform API (Token Plan) and AI-native products (Hailuo AI, MiniMax Code)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results: revenue rose 158.9% from US$30.5 million to US$79.0 million, driven by more capable foundation models and expansion of both monetization channels; revenue generated outside Chinese mainland was approximately 73.0% of the total. Gross profit rose 437.2% to US$20.1 million and gross profit margin increased from 12.2% to 25.4%, primarily driven by improved model and system efficiency and optimization of infrastructure allocation. Loss for the year US$1,871.6 million, mainly a US$1,589.9 million fair value loss on financial liabilities (remeasurement of preferred shares); adjusted net loss (non-IFRS) US$250.9 million (US$244.2 million in 2024).
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue US$79.0 million (+158.9%); gross margin 25.4% (12.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 revenue mix: AI-native products US$53.1 million (+143.4%, 67.2% of revenue), driven by higher user engagement, willingness to pay and monetization of products such as Hailuo AI; Open Platform and other AI-based enterprise services US$26.0 million (+197.8%, 32.8%), fueled by a notable increase in paying customers. R&D expenses rose 33.8% to US$252.8 million, mainly from cloud services expenses related to training activities; selling and distribution expenses fell 40.3% to US$51.9 million as AI-native products grew mainly organically.
quarterly_data.figure: AI-native products US$53.1 million (+143.4%); Open Platform US$26.0 million (+197.8%); R&D US$252.8 million

quarterly_data.signal: Reach: as of December 31, 2025 MiniMax had cumulatively served more than 236 million users across over 200 countries and regions and 214,000 enterprise customers and developers from more than 100 countries and regions; its products include the Open Platform and consumer products MiniMax Agent, Hailuo AI, Talkie and Xingye.
quarterly_data.figure: 236 million users; 214,000 enterprise customers and developers

quarterly_data.signal: Language models: in Q4 2025 MiniMax updated M2, M2.1 and M2-her; the company says M2 became the first Chinese model on OpenRouter to exceed 50 billion tokens in daily consumption. In February 2026 it released M2.5, which it says set a new record on SWE-Bench Verified with a 37% efficiency improvement over M2.1; running continuously for one hour at an output speed of 100 tokens per second costs only one U.S. dollar. In February 2026 average daily token consumption of M2 series text models grew to over six times that of December 2025, with Coding Plan token consumption growing by over ten times.
quarterly_data.figure: M2.5: 37% efficiency gain vs M2.1; daily token consumption over six times December 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Multimodal and agents: video model Hailuo 2.3 (October 2025) with a Fast model that can reduce batch content creation costs by up to 50%; video models had helped creators generate more than 600 million videos by end-2025. Speech 2.6 (October 2025) supports more than 40 languages; users generated over 200 million hours of speech. Music 2.0 and 2.5 handle compositions up to five minutes. In January 2026 MiniMax launched the MiniMax Agent AI-native Workspace; internally its agent interns support nearly 90% of employees.
quarterly_data.figure: More than 600 million videos; over 200 million hours of speech

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (company): MiniMax expects L4 to L5 levels of intelligence to emerge in coding over the coming year and workplace scenarios to follow, and says the demand placed on its platform will expand to an entirely new magnitude. Strategically it will evolve from a foundation-model company into a platform company for the AI era, framing platform value as 'Intelligence Density x Token Throughput', and will enhance scalable infrastructure and token throughput capacity.

Customer and supplier concentration, FY2025: the five largest customers accounted for 18.7% of revenue (2024: 44.1%) and the single largest 12.5% (2024: 30.9%); one customer (a group of entities under common control, unnamed 'Customer A') contributed over 10% of revenue, US$9,868 thousand (2024: US$9,438 thousand). Suppliers are primarily major technology service providers and cloud infrastructure vendors: the five largest accounted for 57.5% of purchases (2024: 57.3%) and the single largest 23.3% (2024: 28.0%); one of the five largest suppliers comprises five subsidiaries of Alisoft China Holding Limited, a substantial shareholder of the company.
quarterly_data.figure: Top five customers 18.7%, largest 12.5% of revenue; top five suppliers 57.5%, largest 23.3% of purchases

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet and other: cash balance US$1,050.3 million at December 31, 2025 (US$880.6 million a year earlier); no significant capital commitments; 415 full-time employees. Contingent liabilities: certain subsidiaries are respondents in several legal dispute cases over claims of alleged infringement of intellectual property rights; the cases are at an early stage and no provision has been made. The Class A shares were listed in Hong Kong on January 9, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Cash balance US$1,050.3 million; 415 full-time employees
